holidays.name: World Teachers' Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate teachers everywhere, from kindergarten finger-paint wranglers to university professors who still use overhead projectors. Students around the world say thanks with apples, cards, and surprisingly heartfelt poems.
holidays.origin: Established by UNESCO in 1994 to commemorate the signing of the 1966 UNESCO/ILO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers.
holidays.funFact: It is celebrated in over 100 countries, and the 1966 recommendation it commemorates was the first international document to set standards for teachers' rights and responsibilities.

holidays.name: National Do Something Nice Day
holidays.description: An unofficial holiday that dares you to commit random acts of kindness, like paying for a stranger's coffee, leaving a compliment on a sticky note, or letting someone merge in traffic without glaring.
holidays.origin: Started as a grassroots feel-good observance in the United States, popularized through social media and calendars of unofficial holidays.
holidays.funFact: Studies on kindness suggest that doing nice things for others can boost your own happiness, so you are basically being selfish by being generous.

holidays.name: National Apple Betty Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble Apple Betty, a baked dessert of spiced apples layered with buttery breadcrumbs. It is basically apple pie's rustic cousin who skipped the crust and showed up to the party anyway.
holidays.origin: The dessert dates back to colonial America, where thrifty cooks used stale bread crumbs and autumn apples to make a warm dessert. The day is a food-calendar observance.
holidays.funFact: Apple Betty is a type of 'brown Betty', a dessert family that was a clever way to use up leftover bread, making it an early example of reducing food waste.

holidays.name: World Cerebral Palsy Day... No, It's Do Something Different? Meet Chic Spy Day: National Kick Butt Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance encouraging people to kick butt at their goals, tackle the tasks they've been procrastinating on, and generally get stuff done, not to be taken in the literal sense.
holidays.origin: An unofficial motivational day that appears on quirky holiday calendars, urging people to push past their excuses in the fall season.
holidays.funFact: Many people use October as a second 'New Year' for goal setting, since the final quarter of the year offers a handy chance to finish strong.

holidays.name: Cinema Day for Gaming? Meet Ada Lovelace-Style Nerd Day: Get Funky Day
holidays.description: A day for letting your inner groove loose by busting out dance moves in the kitchen, the office hallway, or the grocery store aisle, regardless of whether music is playing.
holidays.origin: A playful unofficial observance on novelty holiday calendars, inspired by the funk music tradition that grew from African American communities in the 1960s.
holidays.funFact: Funk pioneer James Brown is often called the 'Godfather of Soul', and his 1965 song 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag' is widely credited with laying the foundation of funk.
